[[File:Kontorovich 2011.jpg|thumb|Alex Kontorovich]]
'''Alex V. Kontorovich''' is an American [[mathematician]] who works in the areas of [[analytic number theory]], [[automorphic forms]] and [[representation theory]], [[L-functions]], [[harmonic analysis]], and homogeneous dynamics.

== Biography ==
Kontorovich earned a bachelor's degree from [[Princeton University]] in 2002, and a PhD from Columbia University in 2007, where he studied under [[Dorian Goldfeld]] and [[Peter Sarnak]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=110727}}</ref> From 2007 to 2010 he was a Tamarkin Assistant Professor at [[Brown University]]. He was later an assistant professor at [[Stony Brook University]] and then assistant professor and associate professor at [[Yale University]]. Since 2014 he has been at [[Rutgers University]], where he is currently a distinguished professor.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~alexk/CVshort.pdf|title=BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH: Alex Kontorovich}}</ref>

Kontorovich has held visiting positions at [[Harvard]], [[ETH Zurich]], and the [[Institute for Advanced Study]]. He served as the editor-in-chief for the journal [[Experimental Mathematics (journal)|''Experimental Mathematics'']], and currently serves as managing editor for the ''Journal of the Association for Mathematical Research''
<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/people/alex-kontorovich|title=Alex Kontorovich bio|publisher=Simons Foundation|access-date=February 23, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://jamathr.org/index.php/jamr/about/editorialTeam|title=Journal of the Association for Mathematical Research — Editorial Team|access-date=February 23, 2024}}</ref> and is an editor for the ''Annals of Formalized Mathematics''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://afm.episciences.org/page/comite-editorial|title=Annals of Formalized Mathematics - Editorial Boards|access-date=June 5, 2025}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
Kontorovich is a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]], elected in the 2017 class of fellows.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows.cgi|title=Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=2024-06-26}}</ref> He was a Sloan Research Fellow from 2013 to 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.yale.edu/2013/03/06/five-yale-scholars-named-sloan-fellows|title=Five Yale scholars named Sloan Fellows|work=Yale News|publisher=Yale University|date=March 6, 2013|first=Eric|last=Gershon|access-date=2024-06-26}}</ref>

In 2014 Kontorovich received the [[Levi L. Conant Prize]] for the paper "From Apollonius to Zaremba: Local-global phenomena in thin orbits".<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://www.ams.org/notices/201404/rnoti-p404.pdf|title=2014 Conant Prize|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|date=April 2014|pages=404–405|first=Elaine|last=Kehoe|volume=61|issue=4}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Kontorovich is the son of Vladimir Kontorovich, an economics professor at [[Haverford College]], and Alla Gil, the former managing director of the investment banking division at [[Goldman Sachs]].<ref name="d596">{{cite | title=Amy Rosen, Alex Kontorovich | date=2008-05-25 | issn=0362-4331 | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/05/25/fashion/weddings/25rosen.html | language=en-US }}</ref><ref name="s809">{{cite web | title=Vladimir Kontorovich | website=Haverford College | date=2002-11-24 | url=https://www.haverford.edu/users/vkontoro }}</ref><ref name="i305">{{cite web | last=Bell | first=Allison | title=Life Insurers Need Better Tools for Detecting Asset Risk: Alla Gil | website=thinkadvisor.com | date=2023-04-27 | url=https://www.thinkadvisor.com/2023/04/27/life-insurers-need-better-tools-for-detecting-asset-risk-alla-gil/ }}</ref> He is married to Amy Rosen Kontorovich, a professor at the [[Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai]].<ref name="d596" /><ref name="d568">{{cite web | title=Amy Kontorovich | website=Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai | url=https://scholars.mssm.edu/en/persons/amy-kontorovich/ }}</ref>

== Selected publications ==
* From Apollonius to Zaremba: Local-global phenomena in thin orbits. ''Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.'' 50 (2013), 187–228. Arxiv<ref>{{cite arXiv | eprint=1208.5460 | last1=Kontorovich | first1=Alex | title=From Apollonius to Zaremba: Local-Global Phenomena in Thin Orbits | date=2012 | class=math.NT }}</ref>
* with [[Jean Bourgain]]: On the Local-Global Conjecture for Apollonian Gaskets. ''Inventiones Mathematicae'' 196 (2014), 589–650. Arxiv<ref>{{cite arXiv | eprint=1205.4416 | last1=Bourgain | first1=Jean | last2=Kontorovich | first2=Alex | title=On the Local-Global Conjecture for integral Apollonian gaskets | date=2012 | class=math.NT }}</ref>
* with Jean Bourgain: On Zaremba's Conjecture. ''Annals of Mathematics'' 180 (2014), 137–196. Arxiv<ref>{{cite arXiv | eprint=1107.3776 | last1=Bourgain | first1=Jean | last2=Kontorovich | first2=Alex | title=On Zaremba's Conjecture | date=2011 | class=math.NT }}</ref>
* with [[Hee Oh]]: Apollonian Packings and Horospheres on Hyperbolic 3-manifolds. ''J. Amer. Math. Soc.'' 24 (2011), 603–648. Arxiv<ref>{{cite arXiv | eprint=0811.2236 | last1=Kontorovich | first1=Alex | last2=Oh | first2=Hee | title=Apollonian circle packings and closed horospheres on hyperbolic 3-manifolds | date=2008 | class=math.DS }}</ref>
* with Hee Oh: Almost Prime Pythagorean Triples in Thin Orbits. ''J. Reine Angew. Math.'' 667 (2012), 89–131. Arxiv<ref>{{cite arXiv | eprint=1001.0370 | last1=Kontorovich | first1=Alex | last2=Oh | first2=Hee | title=Almost prime Pythagorean triples in thin orbits | date=2010 | class=math.NT }}</ref>
